# Annotation LoD Sync Plan

## Problem

Annotations and the MVT canvas overlay show different zoom levels of data for the same geographic area. The `HierarchicalLock` + 2×2 tile grouping causes gaps and suppresses parent-level annotations incorrectly when any child tile is active.

## Solution

Drop `HierarchicalLock` entirely. Register annotation items directly per visible 3D tile. Allow multiple zoom levels of the same feature to coexist; always display the highest-zoom winner.

---

## Changes

### 1. `AnnotationItem` (`ScreenOccupationManager.js`)

Add `zoom = 0` field to the base class constructor. Set it in `MVTAnnotationsPlugin` when creating items (`item.zoom = level`).

---

### 2. `ScreenOccupationManager` — priority-aware dedup

Replace flat `_itemsById: Map<id, item>` with a two-level structure:

- `_itemsById: Map<id, item>` — the current **winner** (highest zoom) in `items[]`
- `_backupItems: Map<id, item[]>` — lower-zoom backups, sorted ascending by zoom

**`register(item)`**
- If no existing for this ID → add to `items[]`, set as winner.
- If existing winner has **lower** zoom → new item is better: copy position from winner, replace winner in `items[]`, push old winner into backups.
- If existing winner has **same or higher** zoom → new item is a backup: insert into `_backupItems[id]` sorted by zoom.

**`unregister(item)`**
- If item is in backups → remove from backup list, done.
- If item is the winner → pop highest-zoom backup (if any), promote it to winner (copy position from old winner for continuity), add to `items[]`. If no backup, remove from `items[]` and `_itemsById`.

---

### 3. `MVTAnnotationsPlugin`

**Remove:**
- `HierarchicalLock` (`this.locks`, all `markActive`/`markInactive` calls)
- `_onLockToggle` callback
- `tileItems: Map<MVT_key, item[]>`
- `_forEach2x2TileInBounds` (no longer needed)

**Add:**
- `tileAnnotations: Map<tile, AnnotationItem[]>` — items registered for each visible 3D tile

**`processTileModel(scene, tile)`** — largely unchanged:
- Still locks content cache tiles so MVT data is available.
- When done, if tile is visible → call `_registerTileAnnotations(tile)`.

**`_onVisibilityChange({ tile, visible })`**
- If `visible` and `info.loaded` → `_registerTileAnnotations(tile)`
- If `!visible` → `_unregisterTileAnnotations(tile)`

**`_registerTileAnnotations(tile)`**
- Compute MVT level: `level = overlay.calculateLevel(info.range)`
- `forEachTileInBounds(info.range, level, tiling, (tx, ty, tl) => { ... })`
- For each feature in `contentCache.get(tx, ty, tl)`:
  - Create `PointAnnotationItem`, set `item.zoom = tl`, `item.id`, `item.lat/lon`, etc.
  - Call `occupancy.register(item)`
- Store items in `tileAnnotations.set(tile, items)`
- Enqueue items for raycasting

**`_unregisterTileAnnotations(tile)`**
- For each item in `tileAnnotations.get(tile)` → `occupancy.unregister(item)`
- `tileAnnotations.delete(tile)`
- Re-enqueue remaining items for raycasting (positions may have changed)

**`disposeTile(tile)`**
- Call `_unregisterTileAnnotations(tile)` if needed
- Release content cache locks (use `forEachTileInBounds`, no 2×2)

---

## What stays the same

- Content cache locking in `processTileModel` (keeps MVT data available)
- `DelayedScreenOccupationManager` — unchanged
- `ready` flag, raycasting queue, `copyPosition` — unchanged
- Canvas overlay — unchanged

---

## Expected result

Parent and child annotations for the same feature coexist during LoD transitions. The higher-zoom item (better raycasted position, finer properties) is always displayed. When the high-zoom tile unloads, the lower-zoom backup surfaces automatically. No gaps, no hierarchical suppression, in sync with the canvas.
